fieldValues.title: Lifecycle states carry full substrate identity
fieldValues.decision_question: When the RFC-006 VocabularyEntry substrate contract and lifecycle.json disagree on what a LifecycleState must carry, which one is right: the contract (id, version and namespace required) or the schema (key only)?
fieldValues.context: The exercise 'Substrate entries: the spec contract and the schemas disagree' (7131fe89, 2026-10-26, release v0.1.0-build.560) found that the RFC-006 substrate contract (srs-spec.md, 'The VocabularyEntry substrate contract') requires id, version and namespace on every entry, LifecycleState included, and says a specialisation MUST NOT relax a required field; lifecycle.json requires only `key` on a state. `repo validate` follows the schema, so srs-programme's governance lifecycle (3c504040) validates clean, while `lifecycle update` follows the contract and refuses it ('state draft is missing required substrate field version'). Re-checked 2026-11-10: the gap has widened; srs-rust#1545 (closed 2026-11-02) made `lifecycle create` enforce the substrate fields too, while lifecycle.json is unchanged. Every lifecycle in the served corpora checked (srs, srs-programme, srs-context, clerk, muDemocracy, srs-web help) has bare key-only states. The exercise also asked whether RelationTypeDefinition carries `aliases` (question 2); that question is parked here (see key_requirements). This is a spec-level ruling: the schema change and corpus migration go through an RFC-006 revision (Door 3) that cites this decision; this record does not override the spec on its own.
fieldValues.friction: No stored lifecycle in the programme can be updated or created through the CLI without an agent hand-inventing id, version and namespace values, which is the file-shape imitation SP-08 describes; meanwhile validation calls the same lifecycles clean (SP-01, spec, schema and tool drifting apart).
fieldValues.alternatives_considered: 1. The contract wins (recommended): lifecycle.json requires id, version and namespace on each state; existing corpora are migrated mechanically (deterministic ids, version 1, the lifecycle's namespace) under a dataModelRevision bump. Leads to: one rule for every substrate entry, states addressable by RFC-006's supersede and retire-by-id, and the write paths srs-rust already ships become correct. 2. The schema wins: amend the contract so a LifecycleState may be keyed only, and relax `lifecycle create`/`update`. Leads to: no migration, but the contract gains its first allowed relaxation, states stay unaddressable by id, and srs-rust#1545 is reverted. 3. Do nothing: validate and write paths keep disagreeing, and every lifecycle edit needs invented values.
fieldValues.key_requirements: One rule per goal: the same entry must not be valid to read and invalid to write. The cost of option 1 is a migration and a dataModelRevision bump across every corpus with bare states; the migration must be mechanical and deterministic so no agent invents values. Option 2 is cheaper now but breaks the contract's own no-relaxation clause and reverts shipped write-path work. Scope: LifecycleState only. Parked: whether RelationTypeDefinition carries `aliases` (exercise question 2) is speculative today; no group issue is blocked by it, and the silent re-key it guards against is tracked separately as srs-rust#1485. The exercise made no recommendation; the option chosen here is the drafter's proposal, for the owner to ratify, edit or set aside.
fieldValues.decision_statement: A lifecycle state carries the full VocabularyEntry substrate identity (id, version and namespace), the same as every other substrate entry.
fieldValues.rationale: Two of the three surfaces (the contract and both write paths) already agree, and the contract forbids a specialisation from relaxing a required field; making the schema match ends the drift with no change to the rule itself. The migration cost is real but one-time and mechanical, whereas relaxing the contract would leave states outside RFC-006's identity rules for good.
fieldValues.revisit_when: The migration cannot assign ids deterministically without collisions or owner choices; or a consumer is found that addresses lifecycle states only by key and would break on the bump; or a relation-type rename is needed and the full-rewrite cost (srs-rust#1485) is actually paid, which reopens the parked aliases question.
fieldValues.next_steps: After ratification: an RFC-006 revision in srs (schema + migration under a revision bump) and the srs-rust validate-side half, filed as linked issues.
